2	
3	*Log S111. Written 29 September 2026 by the one Opus 5.5 agent of log S111. The Avida source and binary stay in the scratch space and are not in the repository; the lines below point into the source at commit 47f13dad (paths under `avida-core/`), so that a reader without the source can see which of Avida's rules the measures lean on. Short excerpts only.*
4	
5	## The build
6	
7	- Source: `github.com/devosoft/avida` at commit 47f13dad ("Merge pull request #95 from mmore500/whole-genome-duplication"), shallow clone; submodule `libs/apto` at its pinned commit 02e18980071d237f1ea4641f3f35cae469e2ed38, fetched with `git submodule update --init --depth 1 libs/apto`. `libs/backward-cpp` and `documentation` not fetched (not needed).
8	- Commands, in `avida/cbuild/`: `AVIDA_DISABLE_BACKTRACE=1 timeout 300 cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ../` then `timeout 1800 nice make -j 3`. Both exited 0 (about 3 minutes). g++ 13.3.0, cmake 3.28.3, Ubuntu 24.04.
9	- **No patch and no extra compiler flag.** 285 compiler warnings (mostly the deprecated `std::binary_function`), no error. The only setting: the environment variable `AVIDA_DISABLE_BACKTRACE=1`, which Avida's own `build_avida` script uses as its fallback; it leaves out the backtrace library.
10	- Result: `cbuild/bin/avida`, "Avida 2.14.0, release build".
11	- One timing run before the plan was written: the default ancestor, seed 1, default settings, 3,000 updates in 104 seconds, 3,594 organisms at the end. Used only to choose run lengths.
12	- The analysis scripts use Python 3 and `numpy` (installed with `pip` for the alignment in `tools/s111_measure_the_worlds_over_time.py`).
13	
14	## Avida's rules the measures lean on
15	
16	| rule | where in the source | what it says |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| A copy error is made by the world, at the moment of copying one instruction | `source/cpu/cHardwareCPU.cc` 7139-7146, `Inst_HeadCopy` | `if (m_organism->TestCopyMut(ctx) ...) { read_inst = m_inst_set->GetRandomInst(ctx); ...}`: with the copy error probability, the instruction written is a random one from the set (which can be the same instruction). The organism's instruction asks for a copy; the error is the world's. |
19	| The random instruction is drawn from the whole set, evenly | `source/cpu/cInstSet.cc` 83-88 | a weighted draw over the set; all weights are equal in the default set. |
20	| Death by age | `source/main/cOrganism.cc` 223-231 | with `DEATH_METHOD 2` (the default), an organism may execute at most `AGE_LIMIT` (20) times its genome length in instructions, then it is removed. With `DEATH_METHOD 0` (control K3, K4) nothing dies of age. |
21	| Where an offspring goes | `avida.cfg`: `BIRTH_METHOD 0`, `PREFER_EMPTY 1` | a random cell next to the parent, an empty one first; otherwise whoever is there is replaced. |
22	| Processor time | `avida.cfg`: `BASE_MERIT_METHOD 4`; `environment.cfg` | merit is proportional to the smaller of the executed and the copied length, multiplied by 2^(task value) for each task performed (`type=pow`); the scheduler hands out instructions in proportion to merit. |
23	| "Viable" in the test processor | `source/cpu/cTestCPU.cc` 282-313 | a program is viable if, run alone, it divides and its offspring is identical to it ("copied true"), or its offspring's line cycles back to it. No mutations are applied there. |
24	| `if-label` | `source/cpu/cHardwareCPU.cc` 6914-6920 | reads the label after it and executes the next instruction only if the last instructions copied are its complement: how the copy loop finds the end. It compares, but only to stop; no instruction of the default set repairs a copied instruction. |
25	| `nop-X` | `source/cpu/cHardwareCPU.cc` 89 (`"True no-operation instruction: does nothing"`, flags 0: no NOP flag) | added as a 27th instruction only for the analysis runs and the control worlds; it does nothing and is not read as part of a label. |
26	| `SAMPLE_OFFSPRING` | `source/analyze/cAnalyze.cc` 1604-1690 | in the test processor, with the world's mutation rates copied in (`test_info.MutationRates().Copy(...GetMutRates())`), one gestation per sample; the offspring genomes are counted. |
27	| `num_breed_true` in `count.dat` | `source/main/cStats.cc` 1099 | the births in the update whose offspring is identical to its parent. |

# S111 build notes, and Avida's rules as read from its source

*Log S111. Written 29 September 2026 by the one Opus 5.5 agent of log S111. The Avida source and binary stay in the scratch space and are not in the repository; the lines below point into the source at commit 47f13dad (paths under `avida-core/`), so that a reader without the source can see which of Avida's rules the measures lean on. Short excerpts only.*

## The build

- Source: `github.com/devosoft/avida` at commit 47f13dad ("Merge pull request #95 from mmore500/whole-genome-duplication"), shallow clone; submodule `libs/apto` at its pinned commit 02e18980071d237f1ea4641f3f35cae469e2ed38, fetched with `git submodule update --init --depth 1 libs/apto`. `libs/backward-cpp` and `documentation` not fetched (not needed).
- Commands, in `avida/cbuild/`: `AVIDA_DISABLE_BACKTRACE=1 timeout 300 cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ../` then `timeout 1800 nice make -j 3`. Both exited 0 (about 3 minutes). g++ 13.3.0, cmake 3.28.3, Ubuntu 24.04.
- **No patch and no extra compiler flag.** 285 compiler warnings (mostly the deprecated `std::binary_function`), no error. The only setting: the environment variable `AVIDA_DISABLE_BACKTRACE=1`, which Avida's own `build_avida` script uses as its fallback; it leaves out the backtrace library.
- Result: `cbuild/bin/avida`, "Avida 2.14.0, release build".
- One timing run before the plan was written: the default ancestor, seed 1, default settings, 3,000 updates in 104 seconds, 3,594 organisms at the end. Used only to choose run lengths.
- The analysis scripts use Python 3 and `numpy` (installed with `pip` for the alignment in `tools/s111_measure_the_worlds_over_time.py`).

## Avida's rules the measures lean on

| rule | where in the source | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| A copy error is made by the world, at the moment of copying one instruction | `source/cpu/cHardwareCPU.cc` 7139-7146, `Inst_HeadCopy` | `if (m_organism->TestCopyMut(ctx) ...) { read_inst = m_inst_set->GetRandomInst(ctx); ...}`: with the copy error probability, the instruction written is a random one from the set (which can be the same instruction). The organism's instruction asks for a copy; the error is the world's. |
| The random instruction is drawn from the whole set, evenly | `source/cpu/cInstSet.cc` 83-88 | a weighted draw over the set; all weights are equal in the default set. |
| Death by age | `source/main/cOrganism.cc` 223-231 | with `DEATH_METHOD 2` (the default), an organism may execute at most `AGE_LIMIT` (20) times its genome length in instructions, then it is removed. With `DEATH_METHOD 0` (control K3, K4) nothing dies of age. |
| Where an offspring goes | `avida.cfg`: `BIRTH_METHOD 0`, `PREFER_EMPTY 1` | a random cell next to the parent, an empty one first; otherwise whoever is there is replaced. |
| Processor time | `avida.cfg`: `BASE_MERIT_METHOD 4`; `environment.cfg` | merit is proportional to the smaller of the executed and the copied length, multiplied by 2^(task value) for each task performed (`type=pow`); the scheduler hands out instructions in proportion to merit. |
| "Viable" in the test processor | `source/cpu/cTestCPU.cc` 282-313 | a program is viable if, run alone, it divides and its offspring is identical to it ("copied true"), or its offspring's line cycles back to it. No mutations are applied there. |
| `if-label` | `source/cpu/cHardwareCPU.cc` 6914-6920 | reads the label after it and executes the next instruction only if the last instructions copied are its complement: how the copy loop finds the end. It compares, but only to stop; no instruction of the default set repairs a copied instruction. |
| `nop-X` | `source/cpu/cHardwareCPU.cc` 89 (`"True no-operation instruction: does nothing"`, flags 0: no NOP flag) | added as a 27th instruction only for the analysis runs and the control worlds; it does nothing and is not read as part of a label. |
| `SAMPLE_OFFSPRING` | `source/analyze/cAnalyze.cc` 1604-1690 | in the test processor, with the world's mutation rates copied in (`test_info.MutationRates().Copy(...GetMutRates())`), one gestation per sample; the offspring genomes are counted. |
| `num_breed_true` in `count.dat` | `source/main/cStats.cc` 1099 | the births in the update whose offspring is identical to its parent. |

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""s112_read_what_the_programs_compute_from_avidas_traces.py
3	
4	What it does, in plain words: for log S112, reads what each evolved program computes, from Avida's own TRACE of the
5	program running alone in the test processor on the fixed inputs. It does not run any program itself: it follows the
6	trace Avida wrote, step by step, and for every register and stack place it keeps a note of where the number there came
7	from (an input read by IO, a constant such as a length written by h-alloc, or an operation such as nand on two earlier
8	numbers). Which registers and stack places each instruction reads and writes is taken from Avida's source
9	(source/cpu/cHardwareCPU.cc, Inst_Nand, Inst_TaskIO, Inst_Swap, Inst_Push, Inst_Pop, ...; the register an instruction
10	acts on is chosen by the nop that follows it, FindModifiedRegister; the stacks as in source/cpu/cCPUStack.h). After every
11	step, the numbers the notes carry are compared with the numbers in the trace; every difference is counted.
12	
13	Each output written by IO is put to Avida's check for the nine sums (source/main/cTaskLib.cc, SetupTests, the "logic id"
14	rule; the lists of ids each sum accepts, lines 513-575). The first accepted output for each sum is compared with the step
15	at which the trace's own count for that sum goes from 0 to 1. Every accepted output is a "route" for the sum; for each
16	route the script records the instructions that made it (with their positions and roles: output write, input read, gate,
17	arithmetic, mover, register choice) and the circuit: the operations from the inputs to the output, with the movers left
18	out, constant parts folded (ZERO, ONES, OTHER), and a canonical form (identical parts merged, operands of nand and add
19	sorted, the three inputs renamed to give the smallest written form).
20	
21	  python3 -B Semantics/tools/s112_read_what_the_programs_compute_from_avidas_traces.py all [jobs]
22	      every living genotype of the nine S111 runs at update 50,000; one JSON line per genotype into the scratch space
23	      (s112/traces/<run>.jsonl); the traces themselves are deleted after reading.
24	  python3 -B Semantics/tools/s112_read_what_the_programs_compute_from_avidas_traces.py one <letters>
25	      one program, printed.
26	
27	Written 30 September 2026 by the one Opus 5.5 agent of log S112.
28	"""
29	import json, os, shutil, sys
30	from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
31	
32	HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
33	sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
34	import s112_run_programs_in_avidas_test_processor as P  # noqa: E402
35	
36	OUT = P.SCRATCH + '/s112/traces'
37	BATCH = 300
38	M32 = 0xffffffff
39	
40	# The ids each sum accepts (cTaskLib.cc 513-575).
41	ACCEPT = {'NOT': {15, 51, 85}, 'NAND': {63, 95, 119}, 'AND': {136, 160, 192},
42	          'ORN': {175, 187, 207, 221, 243, 245}, 'OR': {238, 250, 252}, 'ANDN': {10, 12, 34, 48, 68, 80},
43	          'NOR': {3, 5, 17}, 'XOR': {60, 90, 102}, 'EQU': {153, 165, 195}}
44	REGMOD = {'if-n-equ', 'if-less', 'set-flow', 'shift-r', 'shift-l', 'inc', 'dec', 'push', 'pop', 'swap', 'add', 'sub',
45	          'nand', 'IO', 'nor', 'and', 'or', 'xor'}
46	HEADMOD = {'mov-head', 'jmp-head', 'get-head'}
47	LABEL = {'if-label', 'h-search'}
48	CONTROL = {'if-n-equ', 'if-less', 'if-label', 'mov-head', 'jmp-head', 'get-head', 'set-flow', 'h-search'}
49	COPYING = {'h-copy', 'h-alloc', 'h-divide'}
50	NOPS = {'a': 0, 'b': 1, 'c': 2}
51	
52	
53	def s32(v):
54	    v &= M32
55	    return v - (1 << 32) if v & 0x80000000 else v
56	
57	
58	def logic_id(output, inbuf):
59	    """Avida's SetupTests (cTaskLib.cc 369-448), for an output and the input buffer (most recent first)."""
60	    n = len(inbuf)
61	    ins = [(inbuf[i] & M32) if n > i else 0 for i in range(3)]
62	    out = output & M32
63	    lo = [-1] * 8
64	    for _ in range(32):
65	        pos = sum((ins[i] & 1) << i for i in range(3))
66	        if lo[pos] != -1 and lo[pos] != (out & 1):
67	            return -1
68	        lo[pos] = out & 1
69	        out >>= 1
70	        ins = [x >> 1 for x in ins]
71	    if n < 1:
72	        lo[1] = lo[0]
73	    if n < 2:
74	        lo[2], lo[3] = lo[0], lo[1]
75	    if n < 3:
76	        lo[4], lo[5], lo[6], lo[7] = lo[0], lo[1], lo[2], lo[3]
77	    if min(lo) < 0:
78	        return -2          # a bit combination absent from the inputs (cannot happen with Avida's fixed inputs)
79	    return sum(lo[i] << i for i in range(8))
80	
81	
82	def sums_of(lid):
83	    return [t for t in P.TASKS if lid in ACCEPT[t]]
84	
85	
86	def parse(path):
87	    """Avida's trace file -> list of states (the state before each executed instruction)."""
88	    steps, cur = [], None
89	    for line in open(path):
90	        if line.startswith('---'):
91	            if cur and 'ip' in cur:
92	                steps.append(cur)
93	            cur = {}
94	            continue
95	        if cur is None:
96	            continue
97	        s = line.strip()
98	        if ' IP:' in line and s.split()[0].isdigit():
99	            w = s.split()
100	            cur['cycle'] = int(w[0]); cur['ip'] = int(w[1][3:]); cur['name'] = w[2].strip('()')
101	        elif s.startswith('AX:'):
102	            w = s.split()
103	            cur['regs'] = [int(w[0][3:]), int(w[2][3:]), int(w[4][3:])]
104	        elif s.startswith('R-Head:'):
105	            w = s.split()
106	            cur['heads'] = [int(w[0][7:]), int(w[1][7:]), int(w[2][7:])]
107	        elif 'Stack ' in s and ':' in s:
108	            star = s.startswith('*')
109	            w = s.lstrip('* ').split()
110	            k = int(w[1].rstrip(':'))
111	            cur.setdefault('stacks', [None, None])[k] = [s32(int(x[2:], 16)) for x in w[2:]]
112	            if star:
113	                cur['cur_stack'] = k
114	        elif s.startswith('Mem ('):
115	            cur['mem'] = s.split(':', 1)[1].strip()
116	        elif s.startswith('Task Count'):
117	            w = s.split(':', 1)[1].split()
118	            cur['tasks'] = [int(w[2 * i]) for i in range(9)]
119	        elif s.startswith('Input (env):'):
120	            cur['env'] = [s32(int(x, 16)) for x in s.split(':', 1)[1].split()]
121	        elif s.startswith('Input (buf):'):
122	            cur['buf'] = [s32(int(x, 16)) for x in s.split(':', 1)[1].split()]
123	        elif s.startswith('Output:'):
124	            cur['out'] = [s32(int(x, 16)) for x in s.split(':', 1)[1].split()]
125	    if cur and 'ip' in cur:
126	        steps.append(cur)
127	    return steps
128	
129	
130	class Replay:
131	    """Follows one trace; carries where each number came from; checks against the trace at every step."""
132	
133	    def __init__(self, steps, seq):
134	        self.steps, self.seq, self.L = steps, seq, len(seq)
135	        self.nodes = []                     # each: dict(kind, op, kids, site, mod, cycle, value, ...)
136	        self.mismatch = []                  # (cycle, instruction, what)
137	        self.outputs = []                   # dict(step, cycle, site, mod, reg, node, buf, value)
138	        self.executed = {}                  # site -> set of roles in which it was read or executed
139	        self.control_reads = []             # (site, node) for every register value a control instruction read
140	        self.end = len(steps) - 1           # the step of the first successful split (h-divide), or the last step
141	        self.divided = False
142	        z = self.node('const', value=0, why='start')
143	        self.reg = [z, z, z]
144	        self.stk = [[z] * 10, [z] * 10]
145	
146	    def node(self, kind, value, **kw):
147	        d = dict(kind=kind, value=s32(value), **kw)
148	        self.nodes.append(d)
149	        return len(self.nodes) - 1
150	
151	    def mark(self, site, role):
152	        if site is not None and site < self.L:
153	            self.executed.setdefault(site, set()).add(role)
154	
155	    def run(self):
156	        st = self.steps
157	        for k, s in enumerate(st):
158	            mem, ip, name = s['mem'], s['ip'], s['name']
159	            n = len(mem)
160	            nxt = mem[(ip + 1) % n]
161	            mod = None
162	            if (name in REGMOD or name in HEADMOD) and nxt in NOPS:
163	                mod = (ip + 1) % n
164	            self.mark(ip, name)
165	            if mod is not None:
166	                self.mark(mod, 'modifier of ' + name)
167	            if name in LABEL:
168	                j = ip + 1
169	                while mem[j % n] in NOPS and j - ip <= n:
170	                    self.mark(j % n, 'label of ' + name)
171	                    j += 1
172	            regsel = NOPS[mem[mod]] if mod is not None else None
173	            after = st[k + 1] if k + 1 < len(st) else None
174	            self.step(k, s, after, name, ip, mod, regsel)
175	            if after is None:
176	                self.divided = (name == 'h-divide')      # the trace ends with the split
177	                break
178	            if name == 'h-divide' and len(after['mem']) != len(s['mem']):
179	                # the first successful split ends the program's first run; what follows in the trace file (the
180	                # processor reset, or the offspring's own run) is not part of it
181	                self.end, self.divided = k, True
182	                break
183	            self.check(after, name)
184	
185	    def check(self, after, name):
186	        for r in range(3):
187	            v = self.nodes[self.reg[r]]['value']
188	            if v != after['regs'][r]:
189	                self.mismatch.append((after['cycle'], name, 'register %d' % r))
190	                self.reg[r] = self.node('const', value=after['regs'][r], why='unexplained after ' + name)
191	        for q in range(2):
192	            for i in range(10):
193	                v = self.nodes[self.stk[q][i]]['value']
194	                if v != after['stacks'][q][i]:
195	                    self.mismatch.append((after['cycle'], name, 'stack %d place %d' % (q, i)))
196	                    self.stk[q][i] = self.node('const', value=after['stacks'][q][i], why='unexplained after ' + name)
197	
198	    def step(self, k, s, after, name, ip, mod, regsel):
199	        R = self.reg
200	        cs = s.get('cur_stack', 0)
201	        site = ip if ip < self.L else None
202	        msite = mod if (mod is not None and mod < self.L) else None
203	        BX, CX = 1, 2
204	        if name in ('nand', 'add', 'sub', 'nor', 'and', 'or', 'xor'):
205	            dst = regsel if regsel is not None else BX
206	            a, b = self.nodes[R[BX]]['value'], self.nodes[R[CX]]['value']
207	            v = {'nand': ~(a & b), 'add': a + b, 'sub': a - b, 'nor': ~(a | b), 'and': a & b, 'or': a | b,
208	                 'xor': a ^ b}[name]
209	            R[dst] = self.node('op', value=v, op=name, kids=[R[BX], R[CX]], site=site, mod=msite, cycle=s['cycle'],
210	                               dst=dst)
211	        elif name in ('shift-r', 'shift-l', 'inc', 'dec'):
212	            r = regsel if regsel is not None else BX
213	            a = self.nodes[R[r]]['value']
214	            v = {'shift-r': a >> 1, 'shift-l': a << 1, 'inc': a + 1, 'dec': a - 1}[name]
215	            R[r] = self.node('op', value=v, op=name, kids=[R[r]], site=site, mod=msite, cycle=s['cycle'], dst=r)
216	        elif name == 'swap':
217	            r1 = regsel if regsel is not None else BX
218	            r2 = (r1 + 1) % 3
219	            a, b = R[r1], R[r2]
220	            R[r1] = self.node('wire', value=self.nodes[b]['value'], op='swap', kids=[b], site=site, mod=msite,
221	                              cycle=s['cycle'], dst=r1)
222	            R[r2] = self.node('wire', value=self.nodes[a]['value'], op='swap', kids=[a], site=site, mod=msite,
223	                              cycle=s['cycle'], dst=r2)
224	        elif name == 'push':
225	            r = regsel if regsel is not None else BX
226	            w = self.node('wire', value=self.nodes[R[r]]['value'], op='push', kids=[R[r]], site=site, mod=msite,
227	                          cycle=s['cycle'], stack=cs)
228	            self.stk[cs] = [w] + self.stk[cs][:9]
229	        elif name == 'pop':
230	            r = regsel if regsel is not None else BX
231	            top = self.stk[cs][0]
232	            z = self.node('const', value=0, why='emptied stack place')
233	            self.stk[cs] = self.stk[cs][1:] + [z]
234	            R[r] = self.node('wire', value=self.nodes[top]['value'], op='pop', kids=[top], site=site, mod=msite,
235	                             cycle=s['cycle'], stack=cs, dst=r)
236	        elif name == 'swap-stk':
237	            pass                                   # which stack is current: read from the trace ('*')
238	        elif name == 'IO':
239	            r = regsel if regsel is not None else BX
240	            out_node = R[r]
241	            self.outputs.append(dict(step=k, cycle=s['cycle'], site=site, mod=msite, reg=r, node=out_node,

271	    while stack:
272	        j = stack[-1]

274	            stack.pop()
275	            continue

277	        if d['kind'] in ('in', 'const'):

280	            continue

310	def circuit_terms(nodes, root, names, memo_in, reduce=False, values=False):
311	    """The circuit from root as a table of distinct parts (identical parts merged): wires (movers) skipped, constant
312	    parts folded to ZERO, ONES or OTHER, operands of nand and add in a fixed order. names maps the input index (0, 1, 2
313	    = which of the three numbers handed in) to a leaf name. reduce: steps that leave a number as it is are dropped (add
314	    or sub of ZERO, inc after dec and dec after inc) and nand with ONES is written as nand of the number with itself
315	    (both are NOT). values: OTHER constants are written with their value. Returns (label of root, table) where table
316	    maps each part's label to (operation, labels of its operands); a leaf's label is its name.
317	    (Replaces the first version, which wrote the circuit out as a tree: with parts used many times the written tree
318	    grew too large to hold in memory; see the S112 results, departures.)"""
319	    import hashlib
320	    lab, table = {}, {}
321	    vals = {}
322	    for i in reach(nodes, root):
323	        d = nodes[i]
324	        if d['kind'] == 'wire':
325	            lab[i] = lab[d['kids'][0]]
326	            continue
327	        if d['kind'] == 'in':
328	            lab[i] = names.get(d['which'], 'in?')
329	            continue
330	        if d['kind'] == 'const' or not has_input(nodes, i, memo_in):
331	            r = const_class(d['value'])
332	            lab[i] = ('K%d' % d['value']) if (values and r == 'OTHER') else r
333	            continue
334	        ks = [lab[c] for c in d['kids']]
335	        op = d['op']
336	        r = None
337	        if reduce:
338	            if op == 'add' and 'ZERO' in ks:
339	                r = ks[1] if ks[0] == 'ZERO' else ks[0]
340	            elif op == 'sub' and ks[1] == 'ZERO':
341	                r = ks[0]
342	            elif op in ('inc', 'dec') and ks[0] in table and table[ks[0]][0] == {'inc': 'dec', 'dec': 'inc'}[op]:
343	                r = table[ks[0]][1][0]
344	            elif op == 'nand' and 'ZERO' in ks:
345	                r = 'ONES'
346	            elif op == 'nand' and 'ONES' in ks:
347	                x = ks[1] if ks[0] == 'ONES' else ks[0]
348	                ks = [x, x]
349	        if r is None:
350	            if op in COMMUTATIVE:
351	                ks = sorted(ks)
352	            r = 'h' + hashlib.sha1(('%s(%s)' % (op, ','.join(ks))).encode()).hexdigest()[:20]
353	            table[r] = (op, ks)
354	            vals[r] = d['value']

356	    circuit_terms.values = vals
357	    return lab[root], table

360	def written_form(root, table):
361	    """The circuit written as numbered parts, g1 = nand(x0,x1); g2 = ..., the last part being the output; parts in
362	    order of height (inputs first), ties by label. Returns (written form, number of parts)."""
363	    if root not in table:
364	        return 'out=' + root, 0
365	    seen, stack, order = set(), [root], []
366	    while stack:
367	        h = stack.pop()
368	        if h in seen or h not in table:
369	            continue
370	        seen.add(h)
371	        stack += table[h][1]
372	    height = {}
373	    todo = sorted(seen)
374	    while todo:
375	        rest = []
376	        for h in todo:
377	            ks = [k for k in table[h][1] if k in table]
378	            if all(k in height for k in ks):
379	                height[h] = 1 + max([height[k] for k in ks] or [0])
380	            else:
381	                rest.append(h)
382	        todo = rest
383	    order = sorted(seen, key=lambda h: (height[h], h))
384	    name = {h: 'g%d' % (k + 1) for k, h in enumerate(order)}
385	    parts = ['%s=%s(%s)' % (name[h], table[h][0], ','.join(name.get(k, k) for k in table[h][1])) for h in order]
386	    written_form.order = order
387	    return '; '.join(parts), len(order)

390	def nested_form(root, table, limit=40):
391	    """the same circuit written as one nested expression, if it has at most `limit` operations written out"""
392	    size = {}
393	
394	    def sz(h):
395	        if h not in table:
396	            return 0
397	        if h not in size:
398	            size[h] = 1 + sum(sz(k) for k in table[h][1])
399	        return size[h]
400	    try:
401	        if sz(root) > limit:
402	            return None
403	    except RecursionError:
404	        return None
405	
406	    def f(h):
407	        if h not in table:
408	            return h
409	        op, ks = table[h]
410	        return '%s(%s)' % (op, ','.join(f(k) for k in ks))

512	def recompute(nodes, i, gate, env_new, memo):
513	    """The value node i would have if the gate letter meant `gate` and the inputs were env_new, on the same path.
514	    (Worked earliest node first, without recursion.)"""

523	        elif d['kind'] == 'wire':

525	        else:

527	            op = d['op']
528	            if op == 'nand':

530	            elif op == 'add':

532	            elif op == 'sub':
533	                v = ks[0] - ks[1]
534	            else:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""s112_run_programs_in_avidas_test_processor.py

What it does, in plain words: a helper for log S112. It hands programs (written as letters, one letter per instruction)
to Avida's own analysis mode, which runs each program alone in its private simulated processor (no mutations, no
neighbours), and reads back what Avida reports: whether the program makes an exact copy of itself, and which of the nine
logic sums it does. It can also ask Avida for a TRACE: Avida's own step-by-step record of a program's run (every executed
instruction, the registers, the stacks, the inputs read, the output written, the sums credited so far).

Unlike S111's helper, it can change one thing of the environment before the run: the meaning given to a letter in the
instruction set (e.g. the letter u meaning "nor" instead of "nand"), the whole assignment of meanings to letters, or
the three input numbers the processor hands in. The genomes' letters are never changed by it.

Everything runs in fresh folders in the scratch space, under a time limit; nothing is written into the repository.
Nothing that copies itself runs on the real machine: the copying happens only inside Avida's simulated processor.
Letters: a to z are the 26 instructions of Avida's default set (heads_default); A is nop-X, the do-nothing instruction
used for removals, added as a 27th instruction in these analysis runs only.

Written 30 September 2026 by the one Opus 5.5 agent of log S112.
"""
import os, shutil, subprocess, tempfile

SCRATCH = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ThreadSmith/8d9323da-c0ec-57ec-91fd-8f99ca99320a/scratchpad'
AVIDA = SCRATCH + '/avida/cbuild/bin/avida'
WORK = SCRATCH + '/s112/work'
RUNS = SCRATCH + '/s111/runs'
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
CONF = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(HERE), 'results', 'S111 Avida - the runs', 'configuration')
LETTERS = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
NAMES = ['nop-A', 'nop-B', 'nop-C', 'if-n-equ', 'if-less', 'if-label', 'mov-head', 'jmp-head', 'get-head', 'set-flow',
         'shift-r', 'shift-l', 'inc', 'dec', 'push', 'pop', 'swap-stk', 'swap', 'add', 'sub', 'nand', 'h-copy', 'h-alloc',
         'h-divide', 'IO', 'h-search']
NULL = 'A'
TASKS = ['NOT', 'NAND', 'AND', 'ORN', 'OR', 'ANDN', 'NOR', 'XOR', 'EQU']
FIELDS = ['viable', 'fitness', 'gest_time', 'length', 'exe_length'] + ['task.%d' % i for i in range(9)] + ['sequence']
CHUNK = 4000
FIXED_INPUTS = [0x0f13149f, 0x3308e53e, 0x556241eb]   # Avida's test-processor inputs, cEnvironment.cc 1284-1288
RUN_NAMES = ['main_%s_seed%d' % (c, s) for c in ('low', 'default', 'high') for s in (1, 2, 3)]


def name_of(ch, names=None):
    names = names or NAMES
    return 'nop-X' if ch == NULL else names[LETTERS.index(ch)]


def living(run):
    """All living genotypes of a run at update 50,000: list of (sequence, organisms alive), most common first."""
    path = os.path.join(RUNS, run, 'data', 'detail-50000.spop')
    fmt, out = None, []
    for line in open(path):
        if line.startswith('#format'):
            fmt = line.split()[1:]
            continue
        if line.startswith('#') or not line.strip():
            continue
        r = dict(zip(fmt, line.split()))
        if int(r['num_units']) > 0:
            out.append((r['sequence'], int(r['num_units'])))
    return sorted(out, key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))


def _folder(names=None, with_null=True):
    """A fresh analysis folder; names = the 26 meanings of the letters a..z (default: Avida's default set)."""
    os.makedirs(WORK, exist_ok=True)
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='a_', dir=WORK)
    for f in ['avida.cfg', 'environment.cfg']:
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(CONF, f), d)
    names = names or NAMES
    with open(os.path.join(d, 'instset-heads.cfg'), 'w') as f:
        f.write('INSTSET heads_default:hw_type=0\n\n')
        for k, n in enumerate(names):
            f.write('INST %-12s # %s\n' % (n, LETTERS[k]))
        if with_null:
            f.write('INST nop-X        # A (analysis only: does nothing, is no label)\n')
    with open(os.path.join(d, 'events.cfg'), 'w') as f:
        f.write('u begin Exit\n')
    argv = [AVIDA, '-a', '-s', '1', '-set', 'VERBOSITY', '0']
    return d, argv


def _run(d, argv, lines, timeout):
    with open(os.path.join(d, 'analyze.cfg'), 'w') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
    with open(os.path.join(d, 'analyze.log'), 'w') as log:
        rc = subprocess.run(['timeout', str(timeout), 'nice', '-n', '10'] + argv, cwd=d, stdout=log,
                            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL).returncode
    if rc != 0:
        raise RuntimeError('Avida analysis mode exited %d in %s' % (rc, d))


def _read(path):
    rows = []
    for line in open(path):
        if line.startswith('#') or not line.strip():
            continue
        r = dict(zip(FIELDS, line.split()))
        for k in FIELDS:
            if k != 'sequence':
                r[k] = float(r[k]) if k == 'fitness' else int(float(r[k]))
        rows.append(r)
    return rows


def evaluate(seqs, inputs=None, names=None, with_null=True, timeout=3600):
    """Each sequence run alone in Avida's test processor; one dict per sequence, in order. inputs: three numbers handed
    in instead of the fixed ones (Avida's RECALCULATE manual inputs); names: other meanings for the letters."""
    out = []
    for start in range(0, len(seqs), CHUNK):
        part = seqs[start:start + CHUNK]
        d, argv = _folder(names, with_null)
        rc = 'RECALCULATE' if inputs is None else 'RECALCULATE 0 -1 0 %d %d %d' % tuple(inputs)
        _run(d, argv, ['LOAD_SEQUENCE ' + s for s in part] + [rc, 'DETAIL out.dat ' + ' '.join(FIELDS)], timeout)
        rows = _read(os.path.join(d, 'data', 'out.dat'))
        if len(rows) != len(part) or any(r['sequence'] != s for r, s in zip(rows, part)):
            raise RuntimeError('Avida returned %d rows for %d sequences, or out of order, in %s' % (len(rows), len(part), d))
        out += rows
        shutil.rmtree(d)
    return out


def tasks_of(row):
    return frozenset(t for k, t in enumerate(TASKS) if row['task.%d' % k] > 0)


def trace(seqs, timeout=3600):
    """Avida's TRACE of each sequence on the fixed inputs. Returns (folder, [trace file path per sequence]); the caller
    reads the files and removes the folder."""
    d, argv = _folder()
    _run(d, argv, ['LOAD_SEQUENCE ' + s for s in seqs] + ['TRACE tr/'], timeout)
    paths = [os.path.join(d, 'data', 'tr', 'org-Seq%d.trace' % (k + 1)) for k in range(len(seqs))]
    for p in paths:
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            raise RuntimeError('missing trace %s' % p)
    return d, paths


if __name__ == '__main__':
    pop = living('main_low_seed2')
    s = pop[0][0]
    print(len(pop), s)
    print(evaluate([s, s[:40] + NULL + s[41:]]))
    print(evaluate([s], names=[('nor' if n == 'nand' else n) for n in NAMES]))

1	# S112 What the evolved sums are: what had to be removed, and what it is
2	
3	*Log S112, decisions S60 and S61. Written 30 September 2026 by the one Opus 5.5 agent of log S112 (S56), after the runs, **before the GLM cross-examination**. In the owner's Avida terms (S61, `records/Semantics - Avida terms, given by the owner.md`): an **Avida program** is one program in a program population; a **distinct instruction sequence** is what the plan called a genotype (every Avida program with the same instructions); a **logic task** (the owner's "rudimentary math", the plan's "sum") is one of Avida's nine: NOT, NAND, AND, ORN, OR, ANDN, NOR, XOR, EQU; **task performance** is Avida's test processor crediting the task; **instruction ablation** replaces one instruction by `nop-X`, which does nothing. All entities are digital programs executing on Avida's virtual CPU; nothing biological is involved. The plan, written before running: `results/S112 What the evolved sums are - how it will be found, written before running.md`. The numbers: the `.json` beside this file, written by `tools/s112_summarise_what_had_to_be_removed_and_what_it_is.py`. The exact commands, with every departure: `results/S112 What the evolved sums are - the runs/the exact commands.txt`. Raw output (traces, ablation lists) stays in the scratch space. Observations only; nothing is settled (S28). Nothing in the theory, Part A, Part B, S110 or S111 is written.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 0. The answer, in short
8	
9	The owner asked two things (S60): what had to be removed from the Avida programs that did the logic tasks for them to stop, and what that evolved information is, given the Avida execution environment.
10	
11	**What had to be removed.** For each task, in 98.0% of the program-task pairs (98.6% counted by Avida program) among the programs that perform it and replicate, **one instruction** is enough: there are sites whose single ablation stops the task performance while program replication goes on. These are the program's **required instructions** for that task: on average 5 (NOT, NAND) to 27 (XOR) per program. They are, by kind, mostly `IO` (the instruction that writes a number out and reads the next number in), `nand` (the one logic instruction), `nop-C` and `nop-A` placed right after an instruction (they choose which register it acts on), `swap`, `push`, `pop` (they move numbers between registers and stacks), and for some tasks `add`, `sub`, `inc`, `dec`. By role on Avida's virtual CPU: the reads of the input numbers, the `nand` steps and arithmetic that combine them, the moves and register choices that wire one step to the next, the output write, and **extra `IO` reads that are not on the path at all but set which input number the later reads receive** (Avida hands the three input numbers out in rotation). In the other 2.0%: 1,573 needed a pair of sites (almost always the task has a second route that one ablation leaves standing), two needed a set of three, and 89 (NOT and ORN only, 95 Avida programs) could not be made to stop by ablation while replicating, because every instruction of their task is also an instruction of their replication.
12	
13	**What it is.** In the Avida execution environment, what those instructions make up, when executed, is a **small fixed circuit of the instruction set's operations** from the input reads to the output write: a few `nand` steps, sometimes with `add`, `sub`, `inc`, `dec` steps that on these numbers act bit by bit, applied to the numbers the `IO` channel hands in. For example, the most common circuit of NOT is one `nand` of an input with itself (63% of the NOT programs); of NAND, one `nand` of two inputs (82%); of ORN, `nand(nand(x,y),x)` (69%); of EQU, a five- to eight-step circuit (four circuits cover 81% of the EQU programs). Across all 23,332 distinct instruction sequences of the nine runs, each task has from 35 (XOR) to 409 (OR) distinct circuits (identity steps removed), but a few are run by most programs, and each common circuit is realised by many different instruction strings (the top NOT circuit by 347 different strings of route instructions, in 7,925 distinct sequences). Every circuit that could be computed on all eight combinations of input bits (all but those holding an unnamed constant) gives an output Avida's check accepts for its task, save one.
14	
15	**What it depends on.** It is that circuit only with Avida's meanings for the letters: read the `nand` letter as `nor` and 2% to 84% of the programs still perform a given task, while the rest perform what the circuit then computes (predicted from the trace for 99% of the programs); read it as `and` and 0% to 73% remain; read `IO` as doing nothing and no task is performed by any program; give the 26 letters other meanings and no program replicates or performs anything. With other input numbers of the kind Avida hands out in its worlds, 99% to 100% still perform each task; with fully random 32-bit numbers, 66% to 90%.
16	
17	The rest of this file gives the numbers, the method, worked examples and what is left over.
18	
19	## 1. The programs
20	
21	- **All distinct instruction sequences alive** at update 50,000 in the nine S111 runs (three copy error rates, three seeds): **23,332 sequences, 32,193 Avida programs** (read from each run's `detail-50000.spop`).
22	- Each was run alone in Avida's test processor on Avida's fixed inputs (`0x0f13149f`, `0x3308e53e`, `0x556241eb`, called A, B and C below; every combination of three bits occurs among their 32 bit places). **14,965 sequences (23,813 programs) replicate** in the test processor (Avida's "viable": the copy is exact, or leads back to the program, `cTestCPU.cc` 282-313); **14,719 of them (23,553 programs) perform at least one task**. 8,367 sequences do not replicate; 1,549 of these (1,552 programs) still split off a copy and are credited with tasks (Avida credits the tasks of the last split, `cAnalyzeGenotype.cc` 590); they are counted apart (section 6).
23	- Every count is given by distinct instruction sequence and, where it matters, by Avida program.
24	
25	| task | sequences performing it (replicating) | Avida programs | share of all 32,193 programs | programs Avida's world counted as performing it at update 50,000 |
26	|---|---|---|---|---|
27	| NOT | 12,732 | 21,366 | 66.4% | 29,440 |
28	| NAND | 12,161 | 20,717 | 64.3% | 28,413 |
29	| AND | 7,246 | 11,849 | 36.8% | 17,614 |
30	| ORN | 12,159 | 20,802 | 64.6% | 29,043 |
31	| OR | 10,566 | 19,077 | 59.3% | 27,164 |
32	| ANDN | 11,214 | 19,778 | 61.4% | 28,040 |
33	| NOR | 9,590 | 18,045 | 56.0% | 26,120 |
34	| XOR | 2,673 | 5,782 | 18.0% | 8,652 |
35	| EQU | 5,384 | 10,765 | 33.4% | 16,131 |
36	
37	The world's counts are higher, as S111 found; S111 left the reason unchecked, and it is not checked here either.
38

87	## 3. What it is: the circuits (b)
88	
89	**How.** Avida's own `TRACE` of every sequence on the fixed inputs (analysis mode). A replay follows each trace step by step and carries, for every register and stack place, where its number came from (an input read, a constant, or an operation on earlier numbers), using the register and stack effects of each instruction in Avida's source (`cHardwareCPU.cc`); after every step the carried numbers are compared with the trace. **Steps where the replay's number differs from Avida's trace: 0**, in all 23,332 sequences. Each output an `IO` writes is put to Avida's check (the logic id rule, `cTaskLib.cc` 369-448, with the lists each task accepts, 513-575); every accepted output is a **route** for the task; the first is the one Avida credits, and for **every** performing sequence and task it is the step at which the trace's own task count goes from 0 to 1 (83,725 of 83,725). The tasks the trace credits equal the test processor's for all 14,965 replicating sequences.
90	
91	**The circuit** of a route: the operations from the output back to the input reads, with the movers and register choices left out as wires, constant parts folded to ZERO, ONES (all 32 bits set) or OTHER, identical parts merged, and the three inputs named x0, x1, x2 in the order that gives the smallest written form (so the same circuit on other inputs counts once). The **reduced** form also drops steps that leave a number unchanged (`add` or `sub` of ZERO, `inc` after `dec`, `dec` after `inc`) and writes `nand` with ONES as a `nand` of the number with itself, and `nand` with ZERO as ONES. Each reduced circuit was also computed on the three numbers `0x0f0f0f0f`, `0x33333333`, `0x55555555` (every byte holds all eight combinations of three bits) to read which bit-by-bit function each of its parts is.

132	**The arithmetic steps are exact bit-by-bit identities on 32-bit registers**, not approximations: for example `nand(x,y) + x + 1` equals `x and not y` for every pair of 32-bit numbers (not (x and y) is minus one minus (x and y); adding x and one leaves x minus (x and y), which has no borrow), and `(not x or y) - y` equals `not x and not y` (the bits of y are a subset of those of (not x or y)). 184	## 6. Departures from the plan
185	
186	1. **The trace reader's circuit form.** The first reader wrote each circuit as one nested expression; in programs whose parts are used many times it grew without bound (one worker passed 1.6 GB of memory; an earlier pool broke), and the job was stopped by its exact process numbers. The reader now keeps each circuit as a table of distinct parts (identical parts merged, as the plan asks), works without recursion, folds `nand` with ZERO to ONES in the reduced form, and records each part's logic id. The first run's output from the old reader was set aside unread for results.
187	2. **The shuffled instruction sets (E4)**: Avida refused a set with the `nop` instructions anywhere ("invalid NOP placement"); the shufflings keep the three `nop` meanings among a to c and shuffle the other 23. A few letters keep their meaning by chance (2 to 4 per shuffling).
188	3. **Replication and credit.** The plan says a program that never splits is credited nothing; that holds, but Avida's "viable" means forming a colony, and 1,549 sequences split without replicating and are credited. They are counted apart (section 5). The environment tests are counted over the same replicating performers as the ablations.
189	4. **Added, not planned**: the world's own counts (section 1); the required sites against the credited route; the bit-by-bit check of every reduced circuit on all eight combinations and the grouping by the functions their parts compute; the naming of roles outside the routes (rotation `IO`, stack switch); three reruns in the scratch space for the worked examples (the NOT example's `IO` at 11 and 26, the EQU example's `IO` at 45).
190	5. **Run times**: the pairs took two workers and a four-hour limit (the plan said about 1.5 hours on three); the last run's traces were read again with three workers after one worker went slowly (its programs write many outputs). Nothing else changed.
191	
192	## 7. Tested, not tested, unsure
193	
194	**Tested**: every single ablation of every distinct instruction sequence; every pair among the sites that leave replication, in every replicating performer; triples in the nine most common; Avida's trace of every sequence, replayed with no differing step; the circuits' outputs checked against Avida's task check, on the fixed inputs, on all eight bit combinations, and on 200 other input triples; four kinds of change to the Avida execution environment, with predictions made from the traces.
195	
196	**Not tested**: ablation by deleting an instruction (which shifts every later position) rather than replacing it by `nop-X`; sets of three or more beyond the greedy search (outside the nine most common sequences); task performance outside the test processor (in the world, with neighbours and changing inputs); whether the circuits found are the only ones a program could execute on other inputs (the traces follow one run, on the fixed inputs).
197	
198	**Unsure**: the canonical form names parts by a hash, so two circuits could in principle share a form by collision (not seen; 20 hexadecimal digits); "the same circuit" here means the same operations on the same inputs after identity steps are dropped, and circuits with the same bit-by-bit result but different arithmetic count as different; the role of a required site outside the route is read from what it was executed as, not tested one by one (three reruns only).
199	
200

# S112 What the evolved sums are: what had to be removed, and what it is

*Log S112, decisions S60 and S61. Written 30 September 2026 by the one Opus 5.5 agent of log S112 (S56), after the runs, **before the GLM cross-examination**. In the owner's Avida terms (S61, `records/Semantics - Avida terms, given by the owner.md`): an **Avida program** is one program in a program population; a **distinct instruction sequence** is what the plan called a genotype (every Avida program with the same instructions); a **logic task** (the owner's "rudimentary math", the plan's "sum") is one of Avida's nine: NOT, NAND, AND, ORN, OR, ANDN, NOR, XOR, EQU; **task performance** is Avida's test processor crediting the task; **instruction ablation** replaces one instruction by `nop-X`, which does nothing. All entities are digital programs executing on Avida's virtual CPU; nothing biological is involved. The plan, written before running: `results/S112 What the evolved sums are - how it will be found, written before running.md`. The numbers: the `.json` beside this file, written by `tools/s112_summarise_what_had_to_be_removed_and_what_it_is.py`. The exact commands, with every departure: `results/S112 What the evolved sums are - the runs/the exact commands.txt`. Raw output (traces, ablation lists) stays in the scratch space. Observations only; nothing is settled (S28). Nothing in the theory, Part A, Part B, S110 or S111 is written.*

---

## 0. The answer, in short

The owner asked two things (S60): what had to be removed from the Avida programs that did the logic tasks for them to stop, and what that evolved information is, given the Avida execution environment.

**What had to be removed.** For each task, in 98.0% of the program-task pairs (98.6% counted by Avida program) among the programs that perform it and replicate, **one instruction** is enough: there are sites whose single ablation stops the task performance while program replication goes on. These are the program's **required instructions** for that task: on average 5 (NOT, NAND) to 27 (XOR) per program. They are, by kind, mostly `IO` (the instruction that writes a number out and reads the next number in), `nand` (the one logic instruction), `nop-C` and `nop-A` placed right after an instruction (they choose which register it acts on), `swap`, `push`, `pop` (they move numbers between registers and stacks), and for some tasks `add`, `sub`, `inc`, `dec`. By role on Avida's virtual CPU: the reads of the input numbers, the `nand` steps and arithmetic that combine them, the moves and register choices that wire one step to the next, the output write, and **extra `IO` reads that are not on the path at all but set which input number the later reads receive** (Avida hands the three input numbers out in rotation). In the other 2.0%: 1,573 needed a pair of sites (almost always the task has a second route that one ablation leaves standing), two needed a set of three, and 89 (NOT and ORN only, 95 Avida programs) could not be made to stop by ablation while replicating, because every instruction of their task is also an instruction of their replication.

**What it is.** In the Avida execution environment, what those instructions make up, when executed, is a **small fixed circuit of the instruction set's operations** from the input reads to the output write: a few `nand` steps, sometimes with `add`, `sub`, `inc`, `dec` steps that on these numbers act bit by bit, applied to the numbers the `IO` channel hands in. For example, the most common circuit of NOT is one `nand` of an input with itself (63% of the NOT programs); of NAND, one `nand` of two inputs (82%); of ORN, `nand(nand(x,y),x)` (69%); of EQU, a five- to eight-step circuit (four circuits cover 81% of the EQU programs). Across all 23,332 distinct instruction sequences of the nine runs, each task has from 35 (XOR) to 409 (OR) distinct circuits (identity steps removed), but a few are run by most programs, and each common circuit is realised by many different instruction strings (the top NOT circuit by 347 different strings of route instructions, in 7,925 distinct sequences). Every circuit that could be computed on all eight combinations of input bits (all but those holding an unnamed constant) gives an output Avida's check accepts for its task, save one.

**What it depends on.** It is that circuit only with Avida's meanings for the letters: read the `nand` letter as `nor` and 2% to 84% of the programs still perform a given task, while the rest perform what the circuit then computes (predicted from the trace for 99% of the programs); read it as `and` and 0% to 73% remain; read `IO` as doing nothing and no task is performed by any program; give the 26 letters other meanings and no program replicates or performs anything. With other input numbers of the kind Avida hands out in its worlds, 99% to 100% still perform each task; with fully random 32-bit numbers, 66% to 90%.

The rest of this file gives the numbers, the method, worked examples and what is left over.

## 1. The programs

- **All distinct instruction sequences alive** at update 50,000 in the nine S111 runs (three copy error rates, three seeds): **23,332 sequences, 32,193 Avida programs** (read from each run's `detail-50000.spop`).
- Each was run alone in Avida's test processor on Avida's fixed inputs (`0x0f13149f`, `0x3308e53e`, `0x556241eb`, called A, B and C below; every combination of three bits occurs among their 32 bit places). **14,965 sequences (23,813 programs) replicate** in the test processor (Avida's "viable": the copy is exact, or leads back to the program, `cTestCPU.cc` 282-313); **14,719 of them (23,553 programs) perform at least one task**. 8,367 sequences do not replicate; 1,549 of these (1,552 programs) still split off a copy and are credited with tasks (Avida credits the tasks of the last split, `cAnalyzeGenotype.cc` 590); they are counted apart (section 6).
- Every count is given by distinct instruction sequence and, where it matters, by Avida program.

| task | sequences performing it (replicating) | Avida programs | share of all 32,193 programs | programs Avida's world counted as performing it at update 50,000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NOT | 12,732 | 21,366 | 66.4% | 29,440 |
| NAND | 12,161 | 20,717 | 64.3% | 28,413 |
| AND | 7,246 | 11,849 | 36.8% | 17,614 |
| ORN | 12,159 | 20,802 | 64.6% | 29,043 |
| OR | 10,566 | 19,077 | 59.3% | 27,164 |
| ANDN | 11,214 | 19,778 | 61.4% | 28,040 |
| NOR | 9,590 | 18,045 | 56.0% | 26,120 |
| XOR | 2,673 | 5,782 | 18.0% | 8,652 |
| EQU | 5,384 | 10,765 | 33.4% | 16,131 |

The world's counts are higher, as S111 found; S111 left the reason unchecked, and it is not checked here either.

## 2. What had to be removed (a)

**How.** Every single site of every sequence was ablated (2,330,137 Avida programs run); every pair of sites whose single ablation leaves replication was ablated in every replicating sequence that performs a task (52,428,814 programs run); for the 91 program-task pairs with no stopping set of one or two sites, the irreducible-set search of the plan; for the most common sequence of each run, every triple (836,544 programs run). A set **stops a task** if, with it ablated, the program still replicates in the test processor and the task is no longer credited. A set is **minimal** if no smaller part of it stops the task.

**The smallest set that stops each task:**

| task | size 1 (sequences) | size 2 | size 3 or more | none found | size 1, by Avida programs | required instructions per sequence: mean (range) | distinct strings of required instructions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NOT | 12,014 | 671 | 2 | 45 | 95.5% | 5.2 (0-31) | 1,704 |
| NAND | 11,698 | 463 | 0 | 0 | 97.2% | 5.3 (0-23) | 705 |
| AND | 7,239 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 99.9% | 12.7 (0-34) | 1,184 |
| ORN | 11,850 | 265 | 0 | 44 | 98.4% | 7.1 (0-29) | 1,676 |
| OR | 10,565 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 100.0% | 13.0 (0-29) | 1,361 |
| ANDN | 11,048 | 166 | 0 | 0 | 99.1% | 10.3 (0-36) | 1,553 |
| NOR | 9,590 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 15.8 (3-36) | 1,639 |
| XOR | 2,673 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 27.0 (18-38) | 458 |
| EQU | 5,384 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 21.9 (7-33) | 742 |

Over the nine tasks, 82,061 of 83,725 program-task pairs (98.0%) are stopped by one site. The **required instructions** of a program for a task are the sites whose single ablation stops it; the table's "0" minimum is the programs stopped only by pairs.

**What the required instructions are, by kind** (share of all required sites, over all sequences):

| task | IO | nand | nop-C | swap | nop-A | others above 2% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NOT | 31% | 16% | 18% | 11% | 3% | dec 4%, pop 3%, inc 2%, if-less 2% |
| NAND | 38% | 19% | 23% | 9% | 4% | if-label 3% |
| AND | 30% | 17% | 16% | 9% | 4% | inc 5%, add 5%, pop 3%, if-less 3% |
| ORN | 40% | 21% | 17% | 9% | 3% | if-less 3%, sub 2%, dec 2% |
| OR | 28% | 22% | 20% | 8% | 7% | sub 3%, add 3%, if-label 2%, dec 2% |
| ANDN | 24% | 18% | 20% | 6% | 3% | add 8%, inc 7%, pop 4%, sub 3% |
| NOR | 26% | 19% | 18% | 7% | 6% | add 5%, pop 3%, sub 3%, inc 3% |
| XOR | 24% | 22% | 21% | 7% | 5% | push 5%, pop 5%, swap-stk 3%, sub 2% |
| EQU | 31% | 20% | 20% | 7% | 5% | push 4%, pop 4%, sub 3%, swap-stk 2% |

**By role**, read from Avida's trace of the unablated program (section 3), weighted by Avida programs: for every task the largest roles are the **register choices** (the `nop` read right after an instruction, which picks the register it acts on: 16% to 24%), the **gates** (`nand`: 14% to 21%), the **input reads** (`IO` that brings in a number the circuit uses: 10% to 23%), the **movers** (`swap`, `push`, `pop`: 7% to 16%), **arithmetic** (`add`, `sub`, `inc`, `dec` on the path: 3% to 18%), the **output write** (3% to 13%), and **`IO` outside the routes** (1% to 11%): an `IO` whose own input and output are not on the path, but which takes the next number of Avida's input rotation (`cPopulationCell.h` 214-218: each `IO` reads the next of the three numbers in turn), so that removing it shifts which number every later read receives. Control instructions (`if-less`, `if-label`, `h-search`, jumps) are 1% to 6%, and register or head choices of instructions outside the routes 2% to 9%.

**Required instructions against the route.** 83% of all required sites (a sum over the nine tasks: 751,212 of 904,433) lie in the credited route (the output Avida credits and the instructions that made it, section 3); the other 17% are the `IO` reads that set the rotation, stack switches, control instructions and register choices of instructions outside the route. In the other direction, 50% (NOT) to 85% (EQU) of a credited route's sites are required: the rest can be ablated and the task is performed anyway, most often because another output then carries it (an example in section 2.1).

**What the programs share across runs.** The same kinds and roles, in every run (the two tables above). On Avida's virtual CPU a route's required instructions execute in one order: input reads (with the rotation-setting `IO` among them), then gates and arithmetic with their register choices and the movers between them, then the output write (every worked example in section 3.1 runs so; their positions in the instruction sequence were not compared across all programs). The exact strings differ: 458 (XOR) to 1,704 (NOT) distinct strings of required instructions, in the order of the instruction sequence, for 2,673 to 12,732 sequences.

**Redundancy.** Of the 1,664 program-task pairs that no single site stops, 1,646 have more than one route in the trace (NOT 712 of 718, NAND 452 of 463, ORN 308 of 309, ANDN 166 of 166, AND 7 of 7, OR 1 of 1); a minimal pair then takes out one site of each route (or of the rotation and one route). Pairs also exist beside single sites: minimal pairs total 876,577 over all tasks and programs, in addition to the required instructions. In the most common sequence of each run, exhaustive triples found further minimal sets of size 3 (0 to 254 per task: in default seed 1's, 254 for NOT). So the required instructions are the smallest removals, not the only ones.

### 2.1 Worked examples of what had to be removed

**NOT, low seed 2's most common NOT sequence (44 Avida programs, 110 instructions).** Its route (Avida's trace): site 11 `IO` reads B into register BX; site 12 `push` puts it on the stack; site 16 `pop` (with `nop-C` at 17) puts it into CX; site 20 `nand` computes nand(BX, CX) = nand(B, B) = NOT B into BX; site 21 `swap` moves it to CX; site 26 `IO` (with `nop-C` at 27) writes CX out, which Avida's check accepts as NOT. **Required** (single ablation stops NOT, replication goes on): site 12 `push`, 15 `nop-C` (the register choice of the instruction before it), 20 `nand`, 21 `swap`, 27 `nop-C`. **Not required although on the route**: the input read at 11 (with it ablated, an earlier `IO` in the rotation supplies a number, and NOT of any input is NOT) and the output write at 26 (with it ablated, the NOT value stays in CX and a later `IO`, at site 34, writes out a three-`nand` NOT circuit instead: rerun in the scratch space). So for NOT, what had to be removed is the `nand` that makes it and the wiring that brings one number to both of its operands and its result to the output register. Nine minimal pairs exist beside these five (for example the two `IO` at sites 10 and 11 together).

**EQU, low seed 3's most common EQU sequence (28 Avida programs, 108 instructions).** Required: 25 sites: `IO` at 27, 41, 47, 53, 66 (input reads), `IO` at 45, 51, 55 (outside the route: rotation), `nand` at 43, 75, 78, 91, `add` 60, `inc` 63, `sub` 65, `push` 44, `pop` 90, `swap-stk` 54 and 88 (they decide which stack the `pop` reads), `nop-C` at 28, 61, 67, 76, 79 (register choices), and the output `IO` at 92. No minimal pair. Ablating the rotation `IO` at 45 (rerun): the later reads at 47, 53, 66 get C, B, A instead of A, C, B, and the output at 92 becomes another function (logic id 139), not EQU.

## 3. What it is: the circuits (b)

**How.** Avida's own `TRACE` of every sequence on the fixed inputs (analysis mode). A replay follows each trace step by step and carries, for every register and stack place, where its number came from (an input read, a constant, or an operation on earlier numbers), using the register and stack effects of each instruction in Avida's source (`cHardwareCPU.cc`); after every step the carried numbers are compared with the trace. **Steps where the replay's number differs from Avida's trace: 0**, in all 23,332 sequences. Each output an `IO` writes is put to Avida's check (the logic id rule, `cTaskLib.cc` 369-448, with the lists each task accepts, 513-575); every accepted output is a **route** for the task; the first is the one Avida credits, and for **every** performing sequence and task it is the step at which the trace's own task count goes from 0 to 1 (83,725 of 83,725). The tasks the trace credits equal the test processor's for all 14,965 replicating sequences.

**The circuit** of a route: the operations from the output back to the input reads, with the movers and register choices left out as wires, constant parts folded to ZERO, ONES (all 32 bits set) or OTHER, identical parts merged, and the three inputs named x0, x1, x2 in the order that gives the smallest written form (so the same circuit on other inputs counts once). The **reduced** form also drops steps that leave a number unchanged (`add` or `sub` of ZERO, `inc` after `dec`, `dec` after `inc`) and writes `nand` with ONES as a `nand` of the number with itself, and `nand` with ZERO as ONES. Each reduced circuit was also computed on the three numbers `0x0f0f0f0f`, `0x33333333`, `0x55555555` (every byte holds all eight combinations of three bits) to read which bit-by-bit function each of its parts is.

| task | distinct circuits | distinct reduced circuits | the same, over all routes | smallest possible with `nand` alone | smallest reduced circuit found | smallest `nand`-only circuit found | reduced circuits checked on all 8 bit combinations: accepted / not / not computable (OTHER constant) | credited circuit gives the task for 200 other input triples of the world's kind (sequences) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NOT | 502 | 350 | 1,190 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 250 / 0 / 100 | 12,551 of 12,732 |
| NAND | 326 | 248 | 3,296 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 230 / 0 / 18 | 12,075 of 12,161 |
| AND | 141 | 102 | 151 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 69 / 0 / 33 | 7,154 of 7,246 |
| ORN | 315 | 211 | 17,870 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 174 / 0 / 37 | 12,012 of 12,159 |
| OR | 521 | 409 | 899 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 383 / 0 / 26 | 10,450 of 10,566 |
| ANDN | 246 | 175 | 287 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 139 / 1 / 35 | 11,119 of 11,214 |
| NOR | 242 | 174 | 211 | 4 | 3 (with `sub`) | 4 | 134 / 0 / 40 | 9,476 of 9,590 |
| XOR | 86 | 35 | 42 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 28 / 0 / 7 | 2,661 of 2,673 |
| EQU | 73 | 59 | 72 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 43 / 0 / 16 | 5,346 of 5,384 |

"Over all routes": programs that write several accepted outputs (ORN's loops write it up to hundreds of times) have more circuits than their credited one. The one ANDN circuit not accepted on all eight combinations and the credited circuits below 200 of 200 are circuits whose arithmetic gives the task on Avida's fixed inputs but not on every input (carries between bit places).

**The most common reduced circuits** (x0, x1, x2: the input numbers; share of the Avida programs performing the task; how many distinct sequences and how many distinct strings of route instructions realise it):

| task | circuit (reduced) | in plain logic | programs | sequences | runs | route strings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NOT | `nand(x0,x0)` | not x0 | 63% | 7,925 | 9 | 347 |
| NOT | `sub(ONES,x0)` | minus one minus x0, which is not x0 | 7% | 1,305 | 6 | 155 |
| NAND | `nand(x0,x1)` | not (x0 and x1) | 82% | 8,942 | 9 | 147 |
| NAND | `nand(nand(nand(x0,x1),x0),x0)` | not (x0 and x1), in three steps | 7% | 1,214 | 4 | 17 |
| AND | `inc(add(nand(nand(x0,x1),x0),x0))` | (not x0 or x1), plus x0, plus 1: x0 and x1 | 28% | 1,347 | 4 | 21 |
| AND | `add(inc(nand(nand(x0,x1),x0)),x0)` | the same steps in another order | 20% | 1,482 | 2 | 13 |
| AND | `nand(nand(x0,x1),nand(x0,x1))` | not not (x0 and x1): the two-gate AND | 15% | 1,015 | 5 | 110 |
| ORN | `nand(nand(x0,x1),x0)` | x1 or not x0 | 69% | 7,042 | 9 | 156 |
| ORN | `nand(nand(x0,x0),x1)` | x0 or not x1 | 15% | 2,322 | 9 | 294 |
| OR | `nand(nand(nand(x0,x0),x1),nand(x0,x0))` | x0 or x1, through not x0 and (x0 or not x1) | 17% | 1,987 | 7 | 187 |
| OR | a 6-part circuit with `sub`, `inc`, `add` | x0 or x2; x1 enters and cancels | 15% | 1,005 | 1 | 23 |
| ANDN | `inc(add(nand(x0,x1),x0))` | not (x0 and x1), plus x0, plus 1: x0 and not x1 | 43% | 5,468 | 7 | 101 |
| NOR | a 7-part circuit (not x0 by arithmetic, then x0 or x2, then its `nand` with itself) | not (x0 or x2) | 16% | 968 | 1 | 24 |
| NOR | `sub(nand(nand(x0,x1),x0),x1)` | (not x0 or x1) minus x1: not x0 and not x1 | 15% | 806 | 3 | 24 |
| XOR | a 6-`nand` circuit | x0 xor x1 | 30% | 974 | 1 | 20 |
| XOR | an 8-part circuit (EQU, then `dec` and two `sub`) | x0 xor x1 | 25% | 386 | 1 | 19 |
| XOR | a 7-`nand` circuit | x0 xor x1 | 25% | 922 | 1 | 149 |
| EQU | an 8-part circuit (not x0 by arithmetic, x0 or x2, `nand` with `nand(x0,x2)`) | x0 equals x2, bit by bit | 25% | 880 | 1 | 23 |
| EQU | `nand(nand(x0,x1),nand(nand(nand(x0,x1),x0),sub(nand(nand(x0,x1),x0),x1)))` | x0 equals x1 | 23% | 714 | 1 | 40 |
| EQU | `nand(nand(x0,x1),nand(nand(nand(x0,x0),x1),nand(x0,x0)))` | x0 equals x1, with `nand` alone | 17% | 1,091 | 3 | 55 |

**The arithmetic steps are exact bit-by-bit identities on 32-bit registers**, not approximations: for example `nand(x,y) + x + 1` equals `x and not y` for every pair of 32-bit numbers (not (x and y) is minus one minus (x and y); adding x and one leaves x minus (x and y), which has no borrow), and `(not x or y) - y` equals `not x and not y` (the bits of y are a subset of those of (not x or y)). The credited circuit gives its task for all 200 other input triples in 98.6% to 99.6% of the sequences (table above, last column); the rest hold carries that happen to cancel on Avida's fixed inputs.

**Sharing.** What the programs of one task share is the circuit far more than the instruction string: the top NOT circuit is run by 13,520 Avida programs in 7,925 distinct sequences through 347 distinct route strings; the top NAND circuit by 17,037 programs in 8,942 sequences through 147. The most common circuits of AND, OR, NOR, XOR and EQU are each confined to one to seven runs: each run's program ancestry settled on its own circuits. Grouped by the set of bit-by-bit functions their parts compute (whatever instructions compute them), the reduced circuits fall into 16 (XOR) to 283 (OR) groups.

### 3.1 One worked example per task, in the instruction set's terms and in plain logic

A, B, C are Avida's fixed inputs `0x0f13149f`, `0x3308e53e`, `0x556241eb`; AX, BX, CX the three registers; each line is one executed instruction from Avida's trace, with its site (position in the instruction sequence). The worked program is the most common sequence of the task's most common reduced circuit; its required instructions are listed in the `.json` (`worked_examples`).

- **NOT** (low seed 2, 44 programs): 11 `IO` reads B into BX; 12 `push`; 16 `pop`+`nop-C` puts B into CX; 20 `nand`: BX := nand(B, B) = `0xccf71ac1`; 21 `swap` to CX; 26 `IO`+`nop-C` writes it. Plain logic: **not B**.
- **NAND** (the same sequence): B brought into BX (11, 12, 16, 21); 34 `IO`+`nop-C` reads A into CX; 49 `nand`: BX := nand(B, A) = `0xfcfffbe1`; 51 `swap`; 56 `IO`+`nop-C` writes it. Plain logic: **not (A and B)**.
- **AND** (low seed 1, 27 programs): 39 `IO` reads C into BX; 40 `IO`+`nop-C` reads A into CX; 42 `nand`: nand(C, A) = `0xfafdff74`; 43 `nand`: nand(that, A) = `0xf5eeebeb` (not A or C); 45 `add` A: `0x0502008a`; 47 `inc`: `0x0502008b`; 53 `IO` writes it. Plain logic: **A and C** (`0x0f13149f and 0x556241eb = 0x0502008b`).
- **ORN** (low seed 2, 44 programs): B into BX (11, 12, 16, 21); 26 `IO`+`nop-C` reads C into CX; 28 `nand`+`nop-C`: CX := nand(B, C) = `0xeeffbed5`; 30 `nand`+`nop-C`: CX := nand(B, that) = `0xddf75beb`; 34 `IO`+`nop-C` writes it. Plain logic: **C or not B**.
- **OR** (default seed 1, 12 programs): 33 `IO`+`nop-C` reads A into CX; 41 and 45 `IO` (outside the route: rotation); 47 `IO` reads A into BX; 48 `IO`+`nop-A` reads B into AX; 52 `nand`: BX := nand(A, A) = not A; 61 `swap`+`nop-C` brings B into CX; 63 `nand`+`nop-C`: CX := nand(not A, B) = A or not B; 65 `nand`+`nop-A`: AX := nand(not A, A or not B) = `0x3f1bf5bf`; 69 and 73 `swap`; 78 `IO`+`nop-A` writes AX. Plain logic: **A or B**.
- **ANDN** (low seed 3, 28 programs): 47 `IO`+`nop-C` reads A into CX; 53 `IO` reads C into BX; 57 `nand`: nand(C, A); 60 `add`+`nop-C`: CX := that + A; 63 `inc`+`nop-C`: `0x0a111414`; 66 `IO`+`nop-C` writes it. Plain logic: **A and not C**.
- **NOR** (low seed 3, 28 programs): A and C read (47, 53); 57 `nand`, 60 `add`, 63 `inc`, 65 `sub`: BX := nand(C, A) − (A and not C) = `0xf0eceb60` = not A; 66 `IO`+`nop-C` reads B; 75 `nand`: A or not B; 78 `nand`: A or B = `0x3f1bf5bf`; 81 `push`, 83 `pop`; 85 `nand`: nand(A or B, A or B) = `0xc0e40a40`; 89 `IO` writes it. Plain logic: **not (A or B)**; C enters and cancels.
- **XOR** (default seed 1, 12 programs): 43 `nand`: nand(B, A) (pushed at 44); not A (52), A or not B (63), A or B (65) as for OR; 71 `pop`; 72 `nand`: nand(not (A and B), A or B) = A equals B, `0xc3e40e5e`; 76 `nand`+`nop-C`: nand(A equals B, A or not B) = `0x3c1bf1a1`; 80 `swap`; 82 `IO` writes it. Plain logic: **A xor B**, by way of EQU.
- **EQU** (low seed 3, 28 programs): 43 `nand`: nand(B, A) (pushed at 44); not A by arithmetic as for NOR (57, 60, 63, 65); B read at 66; 75, 78 `nand`: A or B; 90 `pop` (the stack chosen by `swap-stk` at 54 and 88); 91 `nand`: nand(not (A and B), A or B) = `0xc3e40e5e`; 92 `IO` writes it. Plain logic: **A equals B**, bit by bit.

## 4. What it depends on in the Avida execution environment (c)

Each test ran the same instruction sequences (letters unchanged) in the test processor with one thing of the Avida execution environment changed. Counted over the sequences that replicate and perform the task unchanged; "predicted" is the task set the replay computes from each program's own trace with the change applied along the same executed path, made before and independently of the run.

| change | NOT | NAND | AND | ORN | OR | ANDN | NOR | XOR | EQU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| the `nand` letter means `nor` | 79% | 21% | 57% | 17% | 2% | 76% | 84% | 71% | 19% |
| the `nand` letter means `and` | 18% | 1% | 73% | 0% | 0% | 20% | 0% | 0% | 0% |
| `IO` means nothing (`nop-X`) | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% |
| other inputs of the world's kind, 3 triples | 99-100% | 100% | 99% | 99-100% | 99-100% | 100% | 99-100% | 100% | 100% |
| random 32-bit inputs | 85% | 90% | 66% | 77% | 85% | 80% | 84% | 87% | 71% |
| the fixed inputs in another order | 98% | 99% | 87% | 90% | 98% | 98% | 99% | 98% | 98% |
| the 26 meanings given to the letters in another order, 3 shufflings | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% |

- **The meaning of the logic instruction.** With `nand` read as `nor`, 98% to 99% of the programs still replicate, and what they then perform is what their circuits compute with `nor` in place of `nand`: the prediction from the trace matches the test processor for 81,567 of 82,347 program-task pairs (99.1%). Where a circuit is `nand` alone, the task moves to its dual (NAND programs perform NOR: 97%); where arithmetic or a doubled input is in the circuit, it may stay (NOT of x via `nor(x,x)` is still NOT: 79%). With `and`, the prediction matches for 78,782 of 79,266 (99.4%).
- **The input and output channel.** With `IO` doing nothing, no program performs any task; 83% to 89% still replicate (`IO` is not part of their replication).
- **The numbers handed in.** Inputs of the kind Avida hands out in its worlds (the top 8 bits `0x0f`, `0x33`, `0x55`, the rest random): 99% to 100% still perform each task, and the trace prediction matches for 99.99%. Fully random 32-bit inputs: 66% to 90%, and 88% to 93% still replicate; the prediction along the same path matches for 88% (67,517 of 76,805). The difference: most programs' control instructions read numbers made from the inputs (for example comparisons by `if-less`), so other inputs change which instructions run; and circuits with carries give the task only on some inputs.
- **The whole instruction set.** With the 26 meanings reassigned (the three `nop` meanings among the letters a to c, the other 23 among d to z; Avida requires the `nop` instructions first), no program replicates or performs anything.

So the same letters are a circuit for a task only given Avida's meanings for them, its `IO` channel and its rotation of inputs; given those, the circuit gives the task for most input numbers of the world's kind.

## 5. What is left over (d)

- **Not stopped by any ablation found**: 89 program-task pairs (NOT 45, ORN 44; 95 Avida programs, all in two runs), for which ablating every route site that leaves replication, and then every such site in the program, did not stop the task with replication left: their task's instructions (an `IO`, a `nand`, a mover) are all also required for replication (they sit in the replication loop). In two NOT programs the irreducible-set search found sets of size 3 (and 5, 6).
- **Redundancy**: 1,573 program-task pairs need a pair (section 2); the triples in the nine most common sequences show more minimal sets beyond the required instructions. The search is exhaustive only to pairs (to triples in nine sequences).
- **Required sites outside the route**: 17% of the required sites (rotation `IO`, stack switches, control, choices for instructions outside the route).
- **Route sites that are not required**: 15% (EQU) to 50% (NOT) of a credited route's sites: ablating them, the task is performed by another output.
- **Instructions outside every circuit**: over the 14,719 performing sequences' 1,459,777 sites: 437,714 (30%) are in some route of some task (5,477 of these also required for replication), 230,290 (16%) are required for replication only, 720,706 (49%) are executed but in no route and not required for replication, 71,067 (5%) are never executed.
- **Replication-required sites**: their ablation stops the task's credit in 80% of cases (1,081,852 of 1,359,165), because the program no longer splits (a program that never splits is credited nothing); in the traces of each run's most common sequence with one replication-required site ablated, the task outputs are still written in most cases (all tasks in 125 of 159 such traces, some in 24, none in 10). They are part of what stops the credit, not part of the circuit.
- **Programs credited without replicating**: 1,549 sequences (1,552 Avida programs) split but do not replicate and are still credited with tasks; each of them has, for each of its tasks, a single site whose ablation stops the credit. They are outside the counts of sections 2 to 4.
- **Circuits not computable on all eight combinations**: those holding a constant folded as OTHER (100 of NOT's 350 reduced circuits; 7 to 40 for the others); the generality check (200 input triples, computed on the actual numbers) covers them.
- **The trace reading itself**: 0 steps where the replay's number differs from Avida's trace; 0 disagreements between the first accepted output and the trace's own credit.

## 6. Departures from the plan

1. **The trace reader's circuit form.** The first reader wrote each circuit as one nested expression; in programs whose parts are used many times it grew without bound (one worker passed 1.6 GB of memory; an earlier pool broke), and the job was stopped by its exact process numbers. The reader now keeps each circuit as a table of distinct parts (identical parts merged, as the plan asks), works without recursion, folds `nand` with ZERO to ONES in the reduced form, and records each part's logic id. The first run's output from the old reader was set aside unread for results.
2. **The shuffled instruction sets (E4)**: Avida refused a set with the `nop` instructions anywhere ("invalid NOP placement"); the shufflings keep the three `nop` meanings among a to c and shuffle the other 23. A few letters keep their meaning by chance (2 to 4 per shuffling).
3. **Replication and credit.** The plan says a program that never splits is credited nothing; that holds, but Avida's "viable" means forming a colony, and 1,549 sequences split without replicating and are credited. They are counted apart (section 5). The environment tests are counted over the same replicating performers as the ablations.
4. **Added, not planned**: the world's own counts (section 1); the required sites against the credited route; the bit-by-bit check of every reduced circuit on all eight combinations and the grouping by the functions their parts compute; the naming of roles outside the routes (rotation `IO`, stack switch); three reruns in the scratch space for the worked examples (the NOT example's `IO` at 11 and 26, the EQU example's `IO` at 45).
5. **Run times**: the pairs took two workers and a four-hour limit (the plan said about 1.5 hours on three); the last run's traces were read again with three workers after one worker went slowly (its programs write many outputs). Nothing else changed.

## 7. Tested, not tested, unsure

**Tested**: every single ablation of every distinct instruction sequence; every pair among the sites that leave replication, in every replicating performer; triples in the nine most common; Avida's trace of every sequence, replayed with no differing step; the circuits' outputs checked against Avida's task check, on the fixed inputs, on all eight bit combinations, and on 200 other input triples; four kinds of change to the Avida execution environment, with predictions made from the traces.

**Not tested**: ablation by deleting an instruction (which shifts every later position) rather than replacing it by `nop-X`; sets of three or more beyond the greedy search (outside the nine most common sequences); task performance outside the test processor (in the world, with neighbours and changing inputs); whether the circuits found are the only ones a program could execute on other inputs (the traces follow one run, on the fixed inputs).

**Unsure**: the canonical form names parts by a hash, so two circuits could in principle share a form by collision (not seen; 20 hexadecimal digits); "the same circuit" here means the same operations on the same inputs after identity steps are dropped, and circuits with the same bit-by-bit result but different arithmetic count as different; the role of a required site outside the route is read from what it was executed as, not tested one by one (three reruns only).
